Many of us have been promoting the idea of forcing agents like codex-cli/Claude code to do Rocq/Lean proofs, so that "all" bugs can be identified. (yes, the "all" needs caveats). I think it would be great to have a running showcase of documents/software containing bugs that are NOT found when codex/claude is just asked to find bugs but found when they are forced to come up with a proof of correctness in Rocq/Lean. In particular, having simple examples demonstrating this would be great. I did have some relatively simple examples from my blockchain formal verificatiton project that worked in Claude 4.6 but Claude 4.8 finds it even without Rocq/Lean (perhaps the training data for 4.8 has the session from 4.6 where it found the bug while doing a Rocq proof). I do have 1 example (Undefined Behaviour (UB) in C++ code) that still works but it seems complex to explain and it is also not clear whether actual compilers exploit that UB to produce wrong machine code.
(cross posting from Rocq zulip)

The following text-based editor and browser: https://github.com/vkuncak/trubo as of this commit has a bug that involves things like backup files and undo command. What happens is that under certain circumstances you seem to be editing and saving a file from your editor, but the save seems to go to the backup file. Can Claude 4.8 find it? Feel free to file issue based on Claude 4.8 opus review. It's not something that would be easy to spot using formal methods, as one would need to write substantial specifications and, to make this feasible, probably rewrite it (ideally in Lean, which is entirely feasible).
we have some examples in our new blogpost: https://category-labs.github.io/category-research/formalverif/blogs/frontier-models/
